newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Overseas trend pushes Colombo rubber prices down.
newsitem.headline: Overseas trend pushes Colombo rubber prices down.

text.p: Rubber prices were down at the Colombo auction on Friday, where prices were supressed in keeping with excessive overseas supplies, brokers said.
"Wintering, when there is no tapping, has already taken place, so quantities are declining," a leading exporter said. "But despite that we saw supressed prices today."
Brokers said a weakening of overseas markets probably had its effects on the Sri Lankan market, pushing prices down at a time when they should be going up.
There is enough rubber coming from Thailand and Malaysia. Buyers too seem to be pretty well covered. So overseas markets are weak," one broker said.
Best latex one-x, the purest grade, went unquoted on Friday after also being unquoted on Tuesday, when the auction was last held. It last fetched 72 rupees per kilogram.
RSS 1 fetched 63 rupees after going unquoted on Tuesday. Number one gained 10 cents to 70.10 from Tuesday.
On offer were 342 tonnes of crepe and 37 tonnes of sheet rubber. --Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
